messages.subject: TRANSECT vs DISTANCE capabilities
parts:
Hi everyone,

Can anyone tell me what changed between the programs TRANSECT and DISTANCE? I am writing a paper about using distance sampling as a method for surveying arboreal marsupials and am referring to a paper by Kavanagh 1984 Seasonal changes in habitat use by gliders and possums in southeastern New South Wales. This paper reports densities calculated using TRANSECT but then states that "transect counts were not suited to analyses using TRANSECT because the number of animals did not always decrease with distance from the line". However, you can see from the image below (same is attached) that the overall trend is that the number of detections decreases with increasing distance from the transect line. Am I safe in saying that TRANSECT was not equipped to suitably deal with this situation, where as DISTANCE is capable of more robust analysis and capable of dealing with this issue? 

Cheers,
Luke.

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: {Disarmed} RE: {Disarmed} [distance-sampling] TRANSECT vs DISTANCE capabilities
parts:
Luke, that comment from the paper makes no sense at all.  It suggests the writer is completely ignorant of the issue of sampling variation!  TRANSECT probably would have quite happily modelled those data.  TRANSECT had only the Fourier series model (uniform key + cosine adjustments in Distance parlance).  It fitted the model by method of moments, while Distance fits using maximum likelihood.  Yes, Distance has much more flexibility, but no, it would not be right to say that it would model these data adequately, but TRANSECT could not.  The fault is not with TRANSECT but with the statement in the paper.

 

Steve Buckland
